hints: Notice this is the iodoform test, so look for the special group that can be oxidised to a methyl carbonyl.
The positive group in an alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, with the OH on the carbon next to a methyl group.
Check each structure for that $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit and see which one can form $\text{CHI}_3$ on warming.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Think of alkaline aqueous iodine as a test for a very specific little fragment. A yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, means positive.

Test observation:
$$\text{yellow precipitate of CHI}_3 \text{ = positive iodoform test}$$

**Know the two positive groups**

Aldehydes and ketones give a positive result if they contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. Alcohols give a positive result if they contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, because alkaline iodine first oxidises this to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$.

Key link for alcohols:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3$$

**Inspect the four alcohols**

Look for a carbon bearing both OH and a $\text{CH}_3$ group directly attached. Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, butan-2-ol, has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit. The others are primary alcohol without that unit, or tertiary alcohols which cannot be oxidised.

Conclusion:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ gives CHI}_3 \text{ (yellow precipitate)}$$

options.A: Incorrect. $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$ is 2-methylpropan-1-ol, a primary alcohol with $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. It does not contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ and cannot be oxidised to a methyl ketone, so no $\text{CHI}_3$ forms.
options.B: Incorrect. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$ is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol. Tertiary alcohols resist oxidation by this reagent and have no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so the test is negative.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)_2$ is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, also a tertiary alcohol. The C-OH carbon has no H to lose, so it cannot form $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ and gives no yellow precipitate.
options.D: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is butan-2-ol and clearly contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. On warming it is oxidised to $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which then reacts with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ to give yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.
